description: AstroPulse BioSystems is building an offline-first astronaut health telemetry and autonomous triage console for deep-space Artemis/Mars missions. Led by a full-stack Python & wearable HRV/biomedical developer, our app uses NASA-STD-3001 limits and NASA OSDR (OSD-575 Inspiration4) data to deliver instant edge diagnostics, non-doctor crew SOPs, and compressed DTN packets. Seeking collaborators in human factors, clinical validation, or video storytelling.
summary: AstroPulse BioSystems is an offline-first health monitoring prototype for astronauts on long-duration space missions, where distance from Earth can delay access to medical expertise. We developed a mission-control-style console that brings crew vital signs and cabin environmental data together, highlights readings that may need attention, and provides clear self-measurement and response guidance for crew members who are not medical professionals. Interactive mission scenarios demonstrate how the system can help crews recognize changing conditions, such as rising cabin carbon dioxide, and prepare concise telemetry for later transmission when communication is delayed. The project incorporates cited NASA spaceflight health standards and cardiovascular biomarker data from NASA’s Open Science Data Repository. AstroPulse explores how onboard information and practical guidance could help crews respond more confidently while awaiting support from Earth. It is a demonstration prototype, not a certified medical device.
details:
AstroPulse BioSystems is a mission-health decision-support prototype for crews operating far from immediate medical support. Its interactive console brings simulated crew vital signs and cabin-environment readings into one view, applies transparent threshold-based checks, and highlights conditions that may warrant attention. Scenario demonstrations show how crew members could recognize events such as rising cabin CO₂ and follow practical self-measurement and response guidance while waiting for communication with Earth. The prototype also visualizes cardiovascular biomarker data from NASA’s Open Science Data Repository’s Inspiration4 collection and demonstrates how concise telemetry could be queued for delayed transmission.

Built with Python, Streamlit, Plotly, Pandas, and NumPy, AstroPulse explores a human-centered approach to onboard health awareness: clear signals, understandable guidance, and useful information when connectivity is limited. The telemetry and emergency scenarios are simulated; the project is not connected to medical hardware, clinically validated, or a substitute for professional care.
